answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to earn reputation through a slow, verifiable history of useful work before it can transact at full limits. Like light passing through a prism, one identity should split into a verifiable trail of actions, not a crowd of fresh clones. A sable background check, staking a small deposit that is slashed on fraud, raises the cost of mass fakery, while honest agents climb toward the zenith of trust tiers only over time. Sybils can copy code, but they cannot fake months of consistent, attested service.
